stages.name: Roman province of Africa
stages.desc: Africa Proconsularis, ruled from Carthage, garrisoned by the Third Legion

stages.name: Client kingdom of Mauretania
stages.desc: Ruled by Juba II, then Ptolemy, as allies of Rome

stages.name: Held or raided by rebels
stages.desc: Tacfarinas's war zone: Musulamii, Moors and their allies

stages.name: Desert allies of Tacfarinas
stages.desc: Garamantes and desert peoples who sheltered the rebels

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The kingdom of Juba II, Rome's client, with cities at Iol Caesarea and Volubilis
Juba II dies; his son Ptolemy succeeds him
Ptolemy's cavalry joins Dolabella's columns against the rebels

states.name: Libya
timeline: The Garamantes rule the Fezzan; Lepcis, Oea and Sabratha on the coast belong to Rome's province
Tacfarinas raids toward Lepcis and retreats to the Garamantes
The king of the Garamantes sends warriors and takes a share of the plunder

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Africa Proconsularis: Carthage, the old Punic heartland, with the Third Legion at Ammaedara
Tacfarinas raids the province's villages and besieges the fort of Thala
Blaesus's columns and new forts restore Roman control
Dolabella marches out of the province to relieve Thubursicum

states.name: Algeria
timeline: The Musulamii of the high plains around Theveste rise under Tacfarinas; Mazippa's Moors raid
After Camillus's victory the Numidian frontier, then part of the province, falls quiet
Tacfarinas returns, raiding villages and destroying a Roman cohort
Tiberius declares the war won and sends the Ninth Legion away
Tacfarinas besieges Thubursicum and is cornered at Auzia in Mauretania

events.title: Tacfarinas rises
events.text: A Numidian who had served in Rome's auxiliary forces deserts and becomes war leader of the Musulamii.

events.title: Road across pastures
events.text: The military road from Ammaedara to Tacape, finished in AD 14, cuts across seasonal grazing routes, a likely grievance.

events.title: Mazippa's Moors
events.text: Mazippa leads Moorish light horsemen who burn and plunder while Tacfarinas trains his core in Roman fashion.

events.title: The Cinithii join
events.text: The Cinithii, a coastal people near the Lesser Syrtis, are swept into the revolt.

events.title: Third Legion
events.text: Rome's only legion in Africa, the Third Augusta, holds its base at Ammaedara.

events.title: Camillus wins
events.text: The proconsul Furius Camillus meets the rebels in open battle and routs them.

events.title: Camillus honoured
events.text: The Senate votes Camillus triumphal insignia, the highest honour open to a general who was not of the emperor's family.

events.title: Withdrawal south
events.text: Tacfarinas pulls back toward the desert fringe beyond the salt lakes.

events.title: Roman Carthage
events.text: Refounded as a Roman colony under Augustus, Carthage is again the capital of Africa.

events.title: Grain for Rome
events.text: The wheat fields of the Bagradas valley help feed the city of Rome.

events.title: A scholar king
events.text: Juba II, son of a Numidian king and raised in Rome, rules Mauretania from Iol Caesarea.

events.title: Volubilis
events.text: In the far west of Juba's kingdom, Volubilis grows into a walled Berber and Punic town.

events.title: Punic Lepcis
events.text: Lepcis Magna's elite, still speaking Punic, builds a market and theatre with Latin and Punic inscriptions.

events.title: Tacfarinas returns
events.text: Rebuilt with fresh recruits, Tacfarinas raids villages and carries off herds and plunder.

events.title: A cohort routed
events.text: Near the river Pagyda, whose site is unknown, a Roman cohort breaks; its commander Decrius dies fighting.

events.title: Decimation
events.text: The new proconsul Apronius has every tenth man of the disgraced cohort beaten to death.

events.title: Siege of Thala
events.text: Five hundred veterans defend the fort of Thala and drive off Tacfarinas's attack.

events.title: Helvius Rufus
events.text: A common soldier who saved a citizen's life at Thala wins the civic crown from Tiberius.

events.title: Pursuit to the desert
events.text: Apronius's son chases the rebels back toward the desert, without catching them.

events.title: Ninth Legion arrives
events.text: Around this time the Ninth Legion is sent from Pannonia to reinforce the Third.

events.title: Hit and run
events.text: Tacfarinas avoids pitched battle, striking farms and villages and vanishing before the legions arrive.

events.title: Blaesus chosen
events.text: Tiberius asks the Senate to pick a proven general; it chooses Junius Blaesus, uncle of Sejanus.

events.title: Envoys to Tiberius
events.text: Tacfarinas demands land for himself and his army, or endless war; Tiberius is outraged.

events.title: Amnesty
events.text: Blaesus offers pardon to every rebel who lays down arms, except their leader; many surrender.

events.title: Scipio guards Lepcis
events.text: One column blocks the raiders' road to Lepcis and their retreat to the Garamantes.

events.title: Cirta column
events.text: Blaesus's son leads a second column to protect the lands of Cirta.

events.title: Chain of forts
events.text: Blaesus builds forts and keeps campaigning through the winter, giving the rebels no rest.

events.title: Brother captured
events.text: Roman light troops seize Tacfarinas's brother; the rebel leader himself escapes.

events.title: Refuge in the Fezzan
events.text: Tacfarinas's raiders find refuge and a market for plunder among the Garamantes.

events.title: Blaesus hailed imperator
events.text: His troops hail Blaesus as imperator, the last time a general outside the imperial family is so honoured.

events.title: Ninth Legion leaves
events.text: Believing the war over, Tiberius sends the Ninth Legion back to Europe.

events.title: Juba II dies
events.text: The scholar king dies; his young son Ptolemy takes the throne of Mauretania.

events.title: Rebels regroup
events.text: Tacfarinas spreads word that Rome is withdrawing and that its empire is crumbling elsewhere.

events.title: Moors desert Ptolemy
events.text: Angered by the rule of the young king's freedmen, many Moors join Tacfarinas.

events.title: Garamantes aid
events.text: The king of the Garamantes sends warriors and acts as a receiver of the rebels' plunder.

events.title: Siege of Thubursicum
events.text: Tacfarinas besieges a Roman town, probably Thubursicu Numidarum; Dolabella relieves it.

events.title: Chiefs executed
events.text: Dolabella puts to death Musulamian chiefs he suspects of planning to join the revolt.

events.title: Four columns
events.text: With Ptolemy's cavalry, Dolabella splits his army into four columns to sweep the country.

events.title: Death at Auzia
events.text: Surprised at dawn in a half-ruined fort at Auzia, Tacfarinas dies fighting; his son is captured.

events.title: Ptolemy honoured
events.text: Rome sends Ptolemy an ivory sceptre and embroidered robe, hailing him king, ally and friend.

events.title: Garamantes' envoys
events.text: The Garamantes send envoys to Rome to make their peace.

chartNote: Share of the area of four modern countries (today's boundaries), by who held or contested each in a given year. A deliberate simplification: ancient borders cut across these countries, the war moved season by season, and Algeria is coloured by its eastern lands where the fighting was heaviest. Nearly all we know comes from Tacitus, a Roman writing a century later.
